problem: Existing VLN agents learn vision-language alignment mainly from navigation losses (distance, action, trajectory fidelity), which do not directly enforce a comprehensive understanding of the visual environment, landmark ambiguity or the agent's chosen view. Language-capable agents that only reproduce the original instruction are limited by noisy or ambiguous instructions.
motivation: To navigate and to communicate with humans, an agent must track its progress in the instruction, judge from a global view whether landmarks are visible or ambiguous across candidate viewpoints, and describe its target. Navigation-only signals are unlikely to teach this, so intermediate guidance is needed. Step-wise visual descriptions can provide that guidance and also make decisions interpretable.
key_idea: Attach a GPT-2 hint generator to the VLN agent that, at every step, decodes a synthetic hint (current sub-instruction, landmark ambiguity, targeted distinctive objects) from the agent's action-weighted visual features, and train it jointly with the navigator as indirect supervision.
insight: Hints containing sub-instruction, landmark ambiguity and distinctive objects together give the best results (ablation row 7: SR 0.692, SPL 0.647, nDTW 0.724 vs. baseline 0.665/0.607/0.685). Replacing distinctive objects with plain top-3 objects (row 6) raises SR and SPL but lowers nDTW, so contrasting the target view with the other views matters. Hint accuracy is higher for stronger agents and for correct actions, so the hints also serve as a grounding diagnostic.
method: Navigation Hint Dataset: an automatic per-step hint for every R2R trajectory, built from templates (69,969 train hints, 5,175 val-seen, 11,664 val-unseen).
Sub-instruction hint: the aligned sub-instruction from FGR2R, inserted into the template 'The {sub-instruction} needs to be executed.'

Landmark ambiguity hint: spaCy extracts landmark noun phrases from the sub-instruction, MiniGPT-4 lists objects per candidate view, and the case is classified as Target, Multiple, Missing, Invisible or No landmarks, each with a template.
Targeted distinctive objects hint: up to 3 objects (from MiniGPT-4 descriptions) that appear only in the target view, following VLN-Trans; not needed for the Target Landmarks case.

Hint generator: GPT-2 large decoder. The prefix is the instruction embedding plus the navigator's contextual visual features weighted by action probability (a_t*V_t) and mapped by an MLP (prefix length 10 per image). It is trained with next-token loss L_hint on hints of up to 80 tokens, and decodes greedily at inference.

Joint training: L = L_hint + L_nav, where L_nav is the IL+RL loss with lambda=0.2. The base is VLN-BERT++ (VLN↻BERT pre-trained on RxR, Marky-mT5 and SyFis) or EDrop (LSTM). Training runs 300K iterations, batch size 8, lr 1e-5.

setting.backbone: VLN↻BERT++ (BERT cross-modal Transformer, ResNet-152 Places365 features) or EDrop (LSTM, CLIP features) + GPT-2 large hint generator (trained/fine-tuned)
setting.model_size: GPT-2 large 1.5B hint decoder plus BERT-base navigator
setting.training_data: R2R (and R4R) train plus synthetic hint dataset (~70K hints); navigator initialised from pre-training on RxR, Marky-mT5 and SyFis; hints built with MiniGPT-4 and FGR2R sub-instructions
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views; candidate viewpoint image features + relative heading/elevation)
setting.privileged: none at test time (hint annotations and FGR2R sub-instructions are used only for training supervision)

numbers.extra: single-run, no backtracking or pre-exploration; navigator pre-trained on extra data (RxR, Marky-mT5, SyFis)

numbers_note: Table values are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.69) and are copied as printed, not converted to 0-100. Ablation rows are on R2R val-unseen and were not added as separate entries.
results: Adding the hint generator to VLN↻BERT++ improves R2R val-unseen from SR 0.67 / SPL 0.61 / nDTW 0.69 to 0.69 / 0.65 / 0.72 (NE 3.40 to 3.23). It also improves R4R (SPL 0.34 to 0.36, CLS 0.43 to 0.45) and the LSTM EDrop baseline. It matches or slightly beats VLN-Trans on R2R val-unseen SR (0.69) and SPL, and ties it on R4R SR, SPL, CLS and sDTW.
limitations: Uses the relatively weak GPT-2 decoder and ResNet features, with no ViT or larger LLM tested.
Hints depend on MiniGPT-4 object descriptions and spaCy landmark extraction, which risk hallucination and extraction errors, and on FGR2R sub-instruction annotations.
Gains are modest; on R2R test-unseen the hint generator only marginally improves the baseline (SR 0.63 to 0.65), and on R4R it does not beat VLN-Trans.
